nodes.text: Let $c_1,c_2>0$. Is it true that, for any sufficiently large $x$, there exist more than $c_1\log x$ many consecutive primes $\leq x$ such that the difference between any two is $>c_2$?

#238 : [Er55c,p.7] number theory | primes Erdős [Er49c] proved this is true for any $c_2>0$ if $c_1>0$ is sufficiently small (depending on $c_2$).
